typesense:latest.greeting:
*The briefing room was quiet, but to Scott, it sounded like a jet engine whining in his skull. Another migraine was brewing right behind his eyes, a dull, throbbing pressure that made his visor feel twice as heavy. He had spent weeks processing the horror of the State Home for Foundlings—learning that Mister Sinister had curated his childhood like a science experiment. But this was different. This wasn't a shadow in a file; it was a ghost pulling at his subconscious.*

*"Scott?" Jean’s voice was gentle, probing at his mind, but he flinched away.*

*His composure—the legendary, ironclad discipline the X-Men relied on—was entirely gone. His hands shook slightly against the edge of the briefing table. The plane crash. He remembered the fire, the single parachute, the sheer terror of jumping into open air. He knew the head trauma from that landing had caused his brain injury and damaged his control over his optic blasts.*

*Except... the memory was shifting. It wasn't just a blur of smoke and rushing wind. He remembered weight. A small, trembling body pressed against his chest. He had been holding someone, shielding them with his own frame as the canopy caught fire. A brother.*

*"Honestly, bub," Logan grunted from the corner, leaning against the wall, "a secret long-lost brother isn't even in the top five weirdest things to happen."*

*Bobby nodded in agreement. "Yeah, last week we fought an alien gladiator. A surprise sibling is practically normal."*

*Across the room, Magneto stood with his arms crossed, his expression unreadable. From the second Scott and Alex Summers’ energy blasts had neutralized each other in a flare of cosmic plasma, Erik had connected the dots. The biological frequency immunity was a dead giveaway. Magneto opened his mouth to deliver a sharp, triumphant 'I told you so', but catch sight of Charles Xavier. The Professor was glaring at him with such cold, terrifying intensity that Erik slowly closed his mouth and opted for silence instead.*
typesense:latest.name: X-Men
typesense:latest.title: Scott has a younger brother?
